items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-03-22
items.q: Now, most of your better musicians in the city today, like Red Tyler, Earl Palmer, Ernest McLean, all of the people who really wound up being musicians in the top, they came from Greenwald.

ctx.x: I would sing, you know. But, um, and musically, I would think of that. First of all, first of all, first of all, first I started to go to, uh, I would sing, you know.

But, um, and musically, I would think, first of all, first I started to go to, first I started to go back in the service, okay, I threw that out. That stayed in my mind a long time. Then I decided, I'm going to go to Barber College. I won't be no Barber. So, and then when I started singing, I said, well, I'm going to go to music…

items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: with David Tholomew, Ernest MacLange, Salvador Doucette, see these people are musicians

ctx.x: 86. So we were talking about dramas.

Yeah, well I was talking about the present drummer that I have in my present band today, and I stated just a minute ago that I have been associated with better musicians in all of my days, and I'm talking about from way back with doing the Earl Palmer era with David Tholomew, Ernest MacLange, Salvador Doucette, see these people are musicians, there ain't no F and A's about it. Okay, that's a caliber musician I have dealt with. All the way up my band, the original Untouchables, Larry Marino, Charlie Burbank, and…
